column1: # slug|impact,uniqueness,significance,experience,depth|category overrides or -|individual rationale

huai-kha-khaeng-wildlife-sanctuary|9.1,9.5,9.5,8.2,8.3|-|Ecological importance is outstanding; restricted and specialized wildlife encounters cannot be equated with a deep conventional sightseeing visit.
cheow-lan-lake|9.1,9.3,8.5,9.3,8.7|-|Spectacular Khao Sok reservoir and karst scenery, but man-made lake significance and area depth should not match the whole national park.
khao-sok-national-park|9.4,9.4,9.1,9.4,9.3|-|World-class rainforest and limestone scenery, but avoid treating a national park as rare on all dimensions just because landscape is spectacular.
phang-nga-bay|9.4,9.4,8.9,9.3,9.1|-|Striking karst seascape with meaningful exploration, though Ha Long Bay has greater scale and global natural significance.
kaeng-krachan-national-park|9.0,9.2,9.1,8.8,8.9|-|Critical rainforest habitat, while wildlife viewing experience and structured discovery are more variable than biological importance.
khao-yai-national-park|9.0,9.1,9.0,9.0,9.2|-|Major protected landscape and safari-like opportunities, but do not borrow ecological importance entirely into visitor immersion.
hellfire-pass-memorial|8.7,9.0,9.5,8.8,8.1|-|Somber railway history and powerful interpretation; a short memorial walking trail has limited breadth relative to museum ensembles.
wat-phra-mahathat-woramahawihan|8.7,8.9,9.2,8.8,8.2|-|Important active Buddhist religious complex, but the visitor experience is not on the scale of Angkor Wat or the Grand Palace.
phanom-rung-historical-park|9.0,9.4,9.4,9.0,8.6|-|Exceptional Khmer hilltop sanctuary; one temple complex should not inherit the breadth of the Angkor Archaeological Park.
si-thep-historical-park|8.9,9.2,9.4,8.9,8.6|-|Important Dvaravati archaeological landscape, with preservation and on-site depth below the top restored monumental ensembles.
si-satchanalai-historical-park|8.9,9.0,9.3,8.9,8.8|-|Rich Sukhothai-era ruins, but less exceptional multi-site exploration than Ayutthaya or Sukhothai headline parks.
wat-rong-khun-white-temple|8.6,9.1,8.4,8.7,7.6|-|Striking modern artistic temple, whose visual distinctiveness should not be confused with centuries of global historical importance.
maya-bay|8.8,9.1,7.3,8.9,7.4|-|Iconic bay scenery but short visit and relatively replaceable natural significance within global tropical-beach peers.
railay-beach|8.9,9.0,7.5,9.2,8.3|-|Excellent limestone beach and climbing setting; national scenic fame does not imply extraordinary worldwide historical significance.
koh-kradan|8.8,8.9,7.4,9.0,8.4|-|High-quality island beaches but much lower global ecological and historical significance than marine national parks.
similan-islands|9.1,9.3,8.5,9.2,8.9|-|Superb diving islands, but biodiversity and reef experiences should be distinguished from global natural-science uniqueness.
surin-islands|9.0,9.3,8.5,9.2,8.9|-|Marine biodiversity and diving excel, without treating every island group as uniquely world defining.
grand-palace|9.3,9.2,9.5,9.3,9.1|-|Grand Palace is exceptional cultural heritage; individual sections and palaces should not automatically all score near perfect.
wat-pho|9.0,9.2,9.3,9.2,8.5|-|Major temple and reclining Buddha, but one complex does not have the breadth of an entire historic city.

ang-thong-national-marine-park|9.0,9.0,8.6,9.1,8.9|-|The 42-island protected Gulf archipelago offers worthwhile kayaking, overlooks and beaches but is less globally singular and deep than Ha Long Bay; reduce excess environmental significance and visit depth. Source: https://www.thailandtourismdirectory.go.th/en/attraction/2136

ayutthaya-historical-park|9.6,9.5,9.8,9.4,9.5|-|Retain extensive historic royal capital whose surviving monuments have substantive national and world historical impact; distinct from a single Wat ruin. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/576/

ko-phi-phi-leh|9.0,9.1,8.2,9.1,8.3|-|Exceptional iconic limestone island scenery but a constrained island excursion, not an ecosystem-wide national park experience or unique world heritage archipelago; reduce depth/uniqueness and visitor blanket score. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/

sukhothai-historical-park|9.4,9.6,9.8,9.5,9.5|-|Retain heritage significance for Sukhothai core park and monuments of a foundational Thai capital, preserving UNESCO comparison with Ayutthaya without inheriting unrelated towns. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/574

wat-arun|8.9,9.0,8.9,9.1,8.0|-|Highly photogenic Bangkok riverside temple with striking spires, but compact on-site visit and architecture should not inherit entire capital-city heritage significance or breadth of Wat Phra Kaew. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/Attraction/wat-arun-ratchawararam-ratchawaramahawihan

wat-phra-kaew|9.4,9.6,9.8,9.4,8.9|-|Retain extraordinary Bangkok royal temple with Emerald Buddha and sophisticated sacred architecture; distinguish temple footprint from the larger Grand Palace grounds. Source: https://www.royalgrandpalace.th/en/discover/history/

phu-phrabat-historical-park|8.7,9.2,9.4,8.7,8.5|history=9.6,culture=9.4,nature=9.0|Phu Phrabat's 2024 UNESCO Sima stone tradition combines unusual shaped rock shelters, Buddhist ritual markers and older rock art; more globally consequential than a generic modest archeological park but not as extensive as Sukhothai. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

ban-chiang-archaeological-site|8.4,9.2,9.6,8.2,8.1|history=9.8,culture=9.4|UNESCO Ban Chiang documents major prehistoric Southeast Asian settlements, ceramics and bronze metallurgy, warranting substantial historical significance while excavation displays provide more limited immediate visitor spectacle. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

kamphaeng-phet-historical-park|8.5,9.0,9.2,8.7,8.9|history=9.3,architecture=9.2|Kamphaeng Phet is a coherent historic walled settlement and temple zone of the UNESCO Sukhothai serial property; larger ruins offer depth while overall international singularity remains below Sukhothai's core monuments. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

wat-mahathat-sukhothai|8.7,9.1,9.3,8.9,8.0|history=9.5,architecture=9.5|Wat Mahathat is Sukhothai's major central Buddhist sanctuary, a meaningful standalone architecture site, but must not inherit the entire UNESCO historic town's far greater spread of ruins and exploration depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

wat-chaiwatthanaram|8.7,9.0,9.1,8.8,8.0|architecture=9.4,photography=9.3|Impressive riverside Khmer-inspired temple complex is a key Ayutthaya ruin, with strong architectural and photographic appeal yet lower global diversity and reach than the full historic city. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

wat-phra-si-sanphet|8.7,9.1,9.3,8.7,7.9|architecture=9.4,history=9.5|Wat Phra Si Sanphet was a royal ceremonial temple within Ayutthaya and preserves notable chedis, but the site is a fraction of the ancient capital's combined palace and cultural landscape. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

wat-mahathat-ayutthaya|8.6,9.0,9.2,8.7,7.8|history=9.4,photography=9.3|Wat Mahathat is a major Ayutthaya temple famous for Buddha imagery among tree roots; short isolated ruins should not inherit historical-depth scores from the complete UNESCO city. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

wat-si-chum|8.5,8.9,9.0,8.7,7.5|architecture=9.3,history=9.3|The towering seated Buddha in Sukhothai's Wat Si Chum is a distinctive single chapel visit; its iconic image deserves good architecture but limited independent visit depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

phimai-historical-park|8.8,9.3,9.2,8.8,8.6|history=9.4,architecture=9.5|Phimai is an exceptional Khmer temple complex in northeast Thailand, important for Angkor-related architectural history; unlike UNESCO-listed Ayutthaya it is a focused temple sanctuary and is not currently independently inscribed. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/th

doi-inthanon-national-park|9.0,9.0,8.8,9.2,9.4|-|Doi Inthanon contains Thailand's highest summit, montane cloud forest, protected upland bog and several waterfalls and trails, so the entire national park has real multi-site depth rather than just a summit photo stop. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/Articles/forest-bathing-en

tarutao-national-marine-park|9.0,9.2,8.7,9.0,9.0|-|Tarutao is Thailand's first marine national park and encompasses several islands, rainforest, historic prison sites and seasonal snorkeling, but it remains less globally singular than Ha Long Bay. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/Attraction/tarutao-national-park

sanctuary-of-truth|8.8,9.5,8.0,9.2,8.4|architecture=9.7|The Sanctuary of Truth is a striking large hand-carved wooden art building begun only in 1981, with active traditional craftsmanship; its unusual architecture excels but should not be rated as a centuries-old Buddhist royal temple. Source: https://www.thailandtourismdirectory.go.th/en/attraction/1698

khao-luang-national-park|8.7,8.8,8.4,8.7,8.9|-|Khao Luang National Park covers the tallest mountain of southern Thailand with rainforest and multiple waterfalls, but its ecosystems have global rainforest comparators and tourist depth is more specialized than premier wildlife parks. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/Attraction/khao-luang-national-park

wat-phra-that-doi-suthep|8.8,9.0,9.2,9.1,8.3|-|Chiang Mai's major hilltop Lanna Buddhist temple combines an important regional relic shrine with city panoramas and cultural visits; substantial local significance but one temple complex cannot inherit Chiang Mai's full old-city heritage. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/Attraction/wat-phra-that-doi-suthep/

thi-lo-su-waterfall|9.2,9.3,8.5,9.0,8.4|-|Thi Lo Su is among Thailand's most dramatic multi-tier rainforest waterfalls in Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary; natural spectacle deserves very high impact, while a waterfall excursion is less broad than the protected forest system. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/Destinations/West/6

phraya-nakhon-cave|8.9,9.2,8.6,9.1,7.7|-|Phraya Nakhon is a rare sunlit cave with an ornate royal pavilion and a demanding approach walk in Khao Sam Roi Yot, but one cave chamber has far less on-site exploration depth than the entire national park. Source: https://thai.tourismthailand.org/Attraction/%E0%B8%96%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%B3%E0%B8%9E%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%84%E0%B8%A3

ko-tao-island|8.9,8.9,8.0,9.3,9.0|-|Ko Tao is a major Gulf of Thailand diving and snorkeling island with diverse accessible reefs and longer holiday exploration, but diving popularity is not the same as rare worldwide geological or historic significance. Source: https://thailand.go.th/public/visit-thailand-detail/009_113

thailand-burma-railway-centre|8.6,8.8,9.4,9.0,8.4|-|The Thailand–Burma Railway Centre in Kanchanaburi documents the Allied prisoner-of-war forced-labor railway through permanent historical exhibits, meriting serious memorial significance but less depth than the whole Death Railway corridor. Source: https://www.tbrconline.com/visitor.htm

khao-sam-roi-yot-national-park|8.8,8.9,8.5,9.0,8.9|-|Khao Sam Roi Yot encompasses coast, wetlands, limestone peaks and the Phraya Nakhon Cave royal pavilion, offering meaningful park-level exploration without duplicating the cave's separate scenic uniqueness. Source: https://www.tourismthailand.org/Destinations/West/6

wat-phra-that-lampang-luang|8.6,9.0,9.3,8.8,8.3|-|Wat Phra That Lampang Luang preserves a superb walled northern Lanna temple compound with early wooden Buddhist architecture, highly significant regionally but smaller than grand capital shrines. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wat_Phra_That_Lampang_Luang

phra-nang-beach|8.9,9.1,7.2,9.2,8.0|-|Phra Nang Beach has dramatic limestone cliffs, a sea cave and accessible white sand near Railay, an exceptional tropical beach visit but not a worldwide historic monument.

pha-taem-national-park|8.7,9.0,9.1,8.8,9.0|-|Pha Taem combines high Mekong escarpments and prehistoric rock paintings with substantial nature trails, making a more consequential archaeological park than a single riverside lookout. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pha_Taem_National_Park

wat-chedi-luang|8.5,8.7,8.9,8.7,8.1|-|Wat Chedi Luang's monumental partially ruined brick stupa reflects Chiang Mai's Lanna capital history; strong temple significance but a relatively contained city-center visit. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wat_Chedi_Luang

ancient-city-muang-boran|8.4,9.0,7.3,9.0,9.3|-|Ancient Siam Muang Boran is a vast modern open-air park of reconstructed and scaled Thai monuments, giving long visitor depth but replicas must not inherit originals' world archaeological importance.

ko-lipe-island|8.7,8.6,6.6,9.0,8.7|-|Ko Lipe offers walkable tropical beaches, reef snorkeling and small island villages within the Adang-Rawi archipelago, highly enjoyable but less globally irreplaceable than pristine major marine parks. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ko_Lipe

chiang-mai-old-city-moat|8.7,8.5,8.8,9.0,9.0|-|Chiang Mai's walled old-town street grid, surviving moat and historic temple clusters form a coherent long walking experience, far wider than any one chedi or gate.

doi-chiang-dao|8.9,9.1,8.4,9.0,9.0|-|Doi Chiang Dao has dramatic limestone peaks, rare cloud forest and significant local biodiversity, meriting broad hiking appeal but falling short of world-defining high mountain uniqueness. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doi_Chiang_Dao

ko-nang-yuan|8.8,9.2,6.8,9.1,7.5|-|Ko Nang Yuan's three islands linked by a spectacular sandy neck offer iconic snorkeling and viewpoint scenery, but a short boat excursion with limited cultural/historic significance.

phu-kradueng-national-park|8.7,8.8,8.0,9.0,8.9|-|Phu Kradueng's table-mountain plateau demands a long trek with broad forest and cliff vistas, giving far more activity depth than an isolated viewpoint while remaining regionally rather than globally rare. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phu_Kradueng_National_Park

tiger-cave-temple-krabi|8.7,9.0,8.0,9.0,7.6|-|Wat Tham Suea's demanding stairway leads to commanding Krabi karst views and meditation temples, a unique climb-and-shrine experience but less international historical consequence than ancient capitals. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Cave_Temple

chinatown-yaowarat-road|8.7,8.6,8.4,9.1,9.0|-|Bangkok Yaowarat is an extensive living Chinese-Thai commercial and food district with dense streets and temples, richer than one restaurant row but not an intact ancient capital. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinatown%2C_Bangkok

bridge-over-river-kwai|8.5,9.1,9.5,8.6,7.0|-|The bridge near Kanchanaburi represents the Second World War Thailand–Burma Railway and forced-labor tragedy, profound history while the bridge alone remains a short focused monument visit.

wat-phumin|8.6,8.8,8.8,8.6,7.6|-|Nan's Wat Phumin preserves rare nineteenth-century narrative Buddhist murals and an unusual cruciform temple layout, exceptionally meaningful visual heritage within a compact complex. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wat_Phumin

kui-buri-national-park|8.7,8.9,8.5,9.1,8.5|-|Kui Buri National Park is well known for guided wild-elephant and gaur viewing in accessible grasslands, ecologically important but sightings and specialized tours have variable depth. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kui_Buri_National_Park

wat-phra-that-phanom|8.4,8.8,9.0,8.6,7.6|-|Wat Phra That Phanom is a major Mekong-side Thai-Lao Buddhist pilgrimage stupa with long devotional history, but its compact on-site visit is smaller than ancient temple cities. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wat_Phra_That_Phanom

pileh-lagoon|8.9,9.2,6.8,9.0,6.8|-|Pileh Lagoon is an exceptionally scenic enclosed limestone sea inlet on Phi Phi Leh, memorable by boat but a short protected lagoon stop rather than islandwide exploration.

baan-dam-museum|8.7,9.2,8.1,8.8,8.8|-|Chiang Rai's Black House is a complex of contemporary traditional-style dark timber installations and unusual artist collections, engaging as art rather than ancient national heritage. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baandam_Museum

thale-noi-wetland|8.7,9.0,8.9,9.0,8.5|-|Thale Noi's waterbird reserve and seasonal pink lotus fields offer rare freshwater boat photography, with wildlife importance best separated from guaranteed visitor sightings.

wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya|8.6,8.8,8.9,8.7,7.6|-|Wat Ratchaburana preserves an important Ayutthaya prang and royal-burial history, worthwhile temple archaeology but cannot inherit the entire UNESCO historic city's physical extent. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wat_Ratchaburana%2C_Ayutthaya

ko-phi-phi-don|8.7,8.7,6.7,9.0,9.0|-|Phi Phi Don is the larger inhabited island with beaches, dramatic lookouts, snorkeling and a developed village, with much broader travel depth than the narrow Pileh Lagoon stop. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ko_Phi_Phi_Don

bangkok-national-museum|8.8,9.0,9.3,8.9,9.6|-|Bangkok National Museum houses major Thai royal, Buddhist and archaeological collections across an extensive former palace site, meriting real national museum breadth rather than flat mid-eight scores. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangkok_National_Museum

ko-kut-island|8.7,8.6,6.7,9.0,8.7|-|Ko Kut has attractive quiet beaches, coconut forest, waterfalls and small settlements, offering relaxed island exploration without uniquely rare global ecology. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ko_Kut

phra-nakhon-khiri-historical-park|8.4,8.7,8.8,8.7,8.6|-|Phra Nakhon Khiri is a nineteenth-century Thai royal hill palace and temple ensemble above Phetchaburi, a varied royal-architecture excursion smaller than Bangkok's Grand Palace. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phra_Nakhon_Khiri_Historical_Park

wat-phra-singh|8.5,8.8,9.0,8.8,8.0|-|Wat Phra Singh is a key Chiang Mai Lanna Buddhist temple noted for revered Buddha image and ornate assembly halls, strong regional significance with manageable visitor scope. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wat_Phra_Singh

hong-island-krabi|8.8,9.0,6.7,9.1,7.7|-|Hong Island offers a beautiful karst-sided lagoon, white sands and a viewpoint excursion off Krabi, remarkable scenery but less independent scientific/historical breadth than Phang Nga Bay.

phuket-old-town|8.6,8.7,8.5,9.0,8.7|-|Phuket Old Town retains Sino-Portuguese shop-house streets and commercial heritage, appealing as a walking district but smaller and less architecturally defining than major global old cities. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phuket_Old_Town

erawan-national-park|8.8,8.7,8.0,9.1,8.9|-|Erawan National Park's famed seven-tier limestone waterfalls and forest trails make an immersive day hike, with meaningful ecology but not global waterfall-system singularity. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erawan_National_Park

ko-samui-island|8.6,8.5,7.0,9.0,9.2|-|Ko Samui includes multiple beaches, resorts, waterfalls, temples and settlements across a large island, broad tourism depth but less unique natural heritage than marine conservation islands. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ko_Samui
koh-rok-islands|8.5,8.8,7.0,9.0,8.0|-|Ko Rok's paired islands have clear water and strong snorkeling in Mu Ko Lanta marine habitats, excellent remote beaches but a focused marine excursion.

prasat-muang-tam|8.5,8.9,8.9,8.7,8.0|-|Prasat Muang Tam is a carefully planned Khmer sanctuary with carved lintels and water ponds, important ancient architecture independent of but smaller than Phanom Rung. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prasat_Muang_Tam

ko-chang-island|8.7,8.4,7.4,8.9,8.9|-|Ko Chang is a large forested Gulf island with beaches, waterfalls, interior trails and villages, strong varied holiday experience but not globally irreplaceable protected habitat.

samet-nangshe-viewpoint|8.9,9.0,6.5,9.2,6.7|-|Samet Nangshe's elevated panorama of Phang Nga Bay's limestone islets is exceptionally photogenic, but a single hill lookout should not inherit the whole bay's exploration depth.
phu-chi-fa-viewpoint|8.6,8.7,6.9,9.0,7.0|-|Phu Chi Fa is a dramatic east-facing cliff and dawn cloud-sea overlook on Thailand's northern border, outstanding seasonal views but a short summit stop.

sam-phan-bok|8.6,9.0,7.5,8.8,7.2|-|Sam Phan Bok is a field of seasonally exposed Mekong sandstone potholes with distinctive erosional forms, an unusual regional photo landscape but limited independent trail depth.

chatuchak-weekend-market|8.8,8.7,8.3,9.3,9.5|-|Bangkok Chatuchak is an exceptionally large market with thousands of stalls across varied product districts, genuinely deep urban commerce yet not ancient world heritage. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatuchak_Weekend_Market

erawan-waterfalls|8.7,8.7,7.1,9.0,8.0|-|The seven turquoise limestone Erawan cascades are a strong multi-stage forest waterfall outing, with more trail depth than a single plunge pool but less ecology than the entire national park.

wat-phra-that-hariphunchai|8.5,8.8,9.1,8.7,7.8|-|Wat Phra That Hariphunchai is an important Lamphun Lanna Buddhist pilgrimage temple with a large gilded chedi, major regional heritage inside a focused sanctuary. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wat_Phra_That_Hariphunchai

ko-phangan-island|8.6,8.4,6.8,9.0,8.8|-|Ko Phangan offers wide-ranging Gulf beaches, hills and full-moon nightlife, varied vacation depth but cultural fame is not equivalent to rare natural science or historic heritage.

wat-yai-chai-mongkhon|8.5,8.8,8.8,8.8,7.7|-|Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon has a large Ayutthaya chedi and Buddha-lined monastery grounds, a worthwhile stand-alone royal-era temple without the full ancient capital's scale.
